chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), 'When the children were brought to Ali (peace be upon him), he cut their fingertips. From where did he cut?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'From the joint, the joint of the fingertips.'
ai.seo_question: Where exactly did Imam Ali cut the hands of children who committed theft?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the specific judicial application of *qat'* (amputation) for child thieves, with Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifying that the cut occurs at the distal interphalangeal joint of the fingers. This detail highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precision and proportionality in penal jurisprudence, ensuring the punishment is effective yet minimally invasive for those not yet fully liable. It serves as a key reference for understanding how the general rule of hand amputation is adapted for the unique legal status of minors in Islamic law.

en.hubeali: From him, from Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, said,

‘I said to Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), ‘The children, when they came with them, Ali<sup>asws</sup> cut their fingertips from where did he<sup>asws</sup> cut?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From the joints, the joints of the fingertips’.
